title: What If the Moon Disappeared Tonight?
title_it: E se stanotte la Luna sparisse?
idea: At midnight the Moon vanishes. Most people wouldn't notice, but the ocean would: two thirds of the tides' pull is the Moon's, so by morning every tide shrinks to a third; full-moon nights get a hundred times darker, hatchling sea turtles crawl toward the town lights instead of the moonlit sea, the corals wait for a moon that never comes. The twist: the Moon is already leaving, 3.8 cm a year, as fast as fingernails grow, so look up while it's this close; the fox with the lantern already is.
hook: What if the Moon disappeared tonight, at exactly midnight? Most people wouldn't even notice. But the ocean would.
caption: What if the Moon disappeared tonight, at exactly midnight? 🌕 Most people wouldn't notice. The ocean would: two thirds of the pull behind the tides comes from the Moon. And here's the strange part: it's already leaving us, 3.8 cm every year. Which would you miss first: the tides or the moonlight? 🦊🏮
first_comment: Fun fact: the Moon drifts about 3.8 cm farther from Earth every year, measured by bouncing lasers off mirrors the Apollo astronauts left there. 🌕🦊
